This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Ronan.
Democrats say they're planning to focus on lowering cost
and rooting out corruption when they take control
of the House and Senate in January.
NPR's Sam Grindlass reports.
- Democrats say first on their legislative agenda
is restoring enhanced health subsidies
and reversing Medicaid cuts,
reasserting authority over tariffs
and trying to end the Iran war.
On these priorities, Democrats are aligned,
but they'll need help from some Republicans in the Senate
and cooperation from President Trump.
Beyond this early agenda,
Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries,
who's likely the next Speaker of the House,
is promising bold dramatic change,
though what that looks like is not totally clear.
Some newly elected moderate Democrats
are wary of over-promising and under-delivering,
while a new crop of progressives
warn against just tinkering around the edges.
A hundred-plus new members will begin arriving in D.C.
for orientation this weekend.
Sam Grindlass, NPR News, Washington.
- In Austin, Democrats have broken
a three-decade Republican hold
on the governor's office in the state of Texas.
Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott
to become Texas' first Latina governor.
She's promising to work across party lines.
The Texas newsrooms blaze ganey reports.
- Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa
has named former Republican state
lawmaker Ernest Bells to her transition team.
He helped block Governor Greg Abbott's school voucher push,
then lost his 2024 primary to an Abbott-backed challenger.
Hinojosa is promising a bipartisan government
and says she looks forward to working
with Republican leaders in the state legislature.
- People are tired of the divisions, of the fighting,
tired of the culture wars.
This is a time to come together
in a way that is about just delivering for the people of Texas.
- Democrats also won the state house,
but Republicans will still control the state Senate.
I'm Blaise Ganey in Austin.
- The twin ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach
were facing a midnight Pacific time deadline
to reach a contract agreement
with 250 unionized security guards.
The current contract had been extended
while the management group,
the Pacific Maritime Association,
and the ILWU'd negotiate with the help of a federal mediator.
A strike could have a big impact on the U.S. economy
as unionized workers and other bargaining units
are expected to honor those picket lines if they go up.
And it comes as retailers are preparing
for the critical holiday shopping season.
Three weeks after having a portion of a lung removed
during cancer surgery in Rome,
Pope Leo has started a three-nation tour
of the Latin American countries beginning in Uruguay.
The 71-year-old Pope said he felt better
than he looked and he credits God, his medical staff,
and a healthy lifestyle for his quick recovery.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Clean up from the catastrophic flooding this week
in the Blue Ridge Mountains has just begun.
Georgia Public Broadcasting reporter Sophie Grotus
has more on a Georgia town
hit by the unexpected heavy rainfall.
Not one business in downtown McCaysville
was spared from the flooding.
In some restaurants and shops, the water rose over six feet.
The only grocery store is now completely covered in mud.
Volunteers haul out destroyed food and shopping carts.
Now it's about cleanup, but resident Lindsay Teens
worries about the next few months,
typically peak tourism season.
When that doesn't happen, it's devastating for us,
you know, just absolutely devastating.
We depend on every candle sold,
every bag of chips to feed our family.
Both here and Copper Hill, Tennessee
are under states of emergency.
For NPR News, I'm Sophie Grotus in McCaysville, Georgia.
A Venezuelan man who the Department of Homeland Security
says was in the country illegally is in custody
after he was arrested Thursday night near the White House.
The Secret Service said he had multiple weapons
and ammunition in a stolen car
when he was taken into custody
after police believed he was acting suspicious.
Officials also said the man threatened
to kill President Trump and that he heard voices in his head
telling him to come to Washington and shoot the president.
Russian missiles struck Kiev today,
injuring at least five people.
This is Ukraine is preparing for a new round of peace talks
with the U.S. and Russia.
Stocks on Wall Street closed the week with a mixed market.
The Dow was down, the NASDAQ and S&P were up.
I'm Dan Roman, NPR News.

Gina Hinojosa wins Texas governor's race, breaking three-decade Republican hold on the office
Hinojosa names former Republican lawmaker Ernest Bell to her transition team
